evidence: BoundedOutboundHttp.java:45-47 RESPONSE_HEADERS lacks item-retry-after and x-ratelimit-retry; :180 filters response headers by that allowlist
BoundedOutboundHttp is the only OutboundHttp implementation in src/main; PlatformHttpDescriptionWriteAdapter reads response.headers() from it
RetryAfterUnits.java:47-48 expects exactly those native names

V0084__persist_provider_description_retry_timing.sql:60 returns ABSENT when no timing header is present; :76 updates provider_not_before only for KNOWN; :89 states missing timing cannot be certified ABSENT; MO092 gates at :102 and :118

Sales stay scoped to the organization and the object (AdvertisingEvidenceRepository.java:328). The set gates are confirmed: dataDefectOf (AdvertisingCaseCalculationService.java:497-500), evidenceStateOf (:598-600), conversion write-grade (:297), qualification (:551-552, :573-574), CPA only for set variants (AdvertisingEvidenceGatherer.java:232-238, AdvertisingAttributedEconomics.java:59-63, :84), proposal needs a COMPLETE set (AdvertisingProposalService.java:151-158, AdvertisingCandidateRepository.java:118-119), and outcome needs a COMPLETE set (AdvertisingOutcomePlanningService.java:69). Correction 1: when allowable spend is POLICY_BLOCKED it is notAvailable, so Max CPC is absent at AdvertisingCaseCalculationService.java:317-320, not :322-323. Correction 2: on main the parameter was never used. 0f26d0ed created the file (git log --follow shows only 0f26d0ed), and the delegate body first appeared in branch commit 60638b1f. Caveat, not a gap: the cause-bound PROVEN_ADVERTISING_LOSS route drops AD_LINKED_CONVERSION_NOT_WRITE_GRADE (AdActionDependencyPolicy.java:32-35; V0066:21-22). So an object-level loss that includes linked lines outside the set can still produce a decrease-only proposal. That proposal remains bounded by AFFECTED_SET purpose evidence, a COMPLETE-set digest match and the target-policy checks (AdCaseCalculation.java:120-135; V0066:47-49, :52-68) and by the approval chain. This is business semantics, not authorization, tenancy or audit.

alerts.control_input: now in AdvertisingManualPacketRepository.expire(Instant now). This is the time cutoff for expiring manual execution packets. The method calls ops.expire_ad_manual_packets() without passing it (AdvertisingManualPacketRepository.java:83-84).
alerts.enforcement_or_gap: The expiry authority uses the database clock on purpose. The sweep function takes no argument and expires DRAFT, ENDORSED and ISSUED packets where expires_at <= clock_timestamp() (V0060__govern_manual_proposals_packets_and_configuration_proof.sql:410-418). Because a caller cannot supply the time, it cannot move expiry earlier or later. Packet transitions fail closed on expiry even without a sweep: packet.expires_at is copied from proposal.expires_at (V0060:226), ad_manual_proposal_current requires expires_at > statement_timestamp() (V0060:188), and both decide_ad_manual_packet (V0060:244) and start_ad_manual_execution (V0060:266) require that check. No later migration redefines these functions. Java packet writes are also sealed: issue, recordVerification and revoke all throw ACTION_NOT_PERMITTED (AdvertisingManualPacketRepository.java:47-48, 65-66, 71-72).
alerts.note: This alert already existed on main (2026-09-05). Separate observation: no production code calls expire(). The only caller is the test AdvertisingManualShadowIT.java:113, which passes year 9999 and asserts only >= 0. As a result, a packet past its expiry can still show a pre-expiry state when read, but every state change is refused on database time. This is display staleness, not a control gap.

adversarial_verification.evidence: The classification stands, but one side claim needs correcting. Ignoring `now` protects the system on purpose. ops.expire_ad_manual_packets() takes no argument and uses clock_timestamp() (V0060:411-418), and AdvertisingManualShadowIT.java:112 states the intent: a caller cannot expire live instructions by picking a distant clock. Every transition refuses an expired packet using database time. expires_at is copied from the proposal (V0060:226). ad_manual_proposal_current requires expires_at>statement_timestamp() (V0060:188). decide_ad_manual_packet and start_ad_manual_execution both require that check (V0060:244, :266). Observation recording needs execution already started (V0060:312-316). Java issue/recordVerification/revoke all throw (AdvertisingManualPacketRepository.java:47-48, 65-66, 71-72). The UI and projection also check expiry (AdvertisingDisclosureService.java:298-300; ManualExecutionPacketView.java:128-130; AdvertisingExceptionService.java:294). ops.take_ad_action_reservation's CONFIRMED_MANUAL_PACKET branch checks state='MANUAL_PACKET_ISSUED' without checking expiry (V0058:719-721), and it is granted to marketops_app (V0058:740). However, its only production invoker is start_ad_manual_execution (V0060:279), which checks expiry first, and the only Java caller passes CONTROLLED_AD_BID_CHANGE (AdvertisingDecisionService.java:215). A reservation is also only a hold: it does not change the packet's state or authorize anything. CORRECTION to the note: the effect is more than stale display. No @Scheduled method or other production code calls expire() (AdvertisingRecalculationScheduler.java:76-133 has no sweep; the only callers are tests). As a result, an expired, unstarted MANUAL_PACKET_ISSUED packet keeps its place in the per-object live-instruction unique index (V0073:8-9) and the issue guard (V0073:13-18). While it stays there, no new manual packet for that ad_native_object_id can reach ISSUED. It is cleared only by containment activation (V0058:898-905) or a human-authority-change revocation (V0058:1899-1902). This is a liveness block that fails closed, not a weakened control, and honoring `now` would not fix it because nothing calls the method. It belongs as a separate registration: the missing production expiry sweep.

alerts.enforcement_or_gap: The only caller is ApprovalService.reject (ApprovalService.java:168-187), in one transaction. That caller already enforces every control this id could serve. Authorization: requireDecidable (:171, :264-282) requires LISTING_ACTION_APPROVE_MATERIAL/ORDINARY at store scope (:267-268, :298-305), plus expectedVersion (:269), READY_FOR_REVIEW state (:272) and freshness (:278). alerts.note: Separate from this alert, recordRejection ignores the boolean from moveAction (ListingActionDecisionService.java:275; the UPDATE is version-guarded at ListingActionRepository.java:340-345). After a concurrent version bump the lc_action could stay REVIEWED while the recommendation is REJECTED. Every approval and launch gate above still refuses it, so this is a consistency and maintenance item, not a bypass. The same method also uses clock.instant() rather than databaseNow(). One-sentence option: either drop the parameter, or persist it on the cancellation and raise VERSION_CONFLICT when moveAction returns false.

adversarial_verification.evidence: Checked at 57c5efc4. I could not find a bypass. The only implementation is ListingActionDecisionService.java:39; recordRejection is at :272-278, and :275 ignores the id and the boolean. The only caller is ApprovalService.java:182. Authorization: requireDecidable requires the store-scope approve grant (:267-268, 298-305), the version (:269), READY_FOR_REVIEW (:272) and freshness (:278). RecommendationService.require (:209-213) does not filter by org, but tenancy still holds at JdbcBusinessAuthorization.java:112. Attribution: record() inserts the decision with decided_by_user_id and writes APPROVAL_DECISION audit (ApprovalService.java:316-336). V0018:205-207 requires a human actor on REJECTED rows. The BEFORE INSERT trigger stamps authority_snapshot (V0077:1475-1498; trigger V0020:480). Terminality: REJECTED is terminal in Java (RecommendationState.java:61, :81), and the recommendation transition is version-guarded (RecommendationRepository.java:135). Launch is still blocked. APPROVED needs a BOUND binding in the DB (V0077:1371-1373). Bindings are only inserted by bindApproval (ListingActionDecisionService.java:260), and its only caller is the approve path (ApprovalService.java:159). The DB launch also needs a binding and APPROVED state (V0118:124-128). The listing task links the decision via "approval-decision:"+decisionId (ApprovalService.java:183-184). Two refinements, neither a control gap. (1) Audit completeness: the rejection-driven lc_action DRAFT/REVIEWED->CANCELLED move writes no lc_action-entity STATUS_CHANGE audit and does not store the decision id. ListingActionService.cancel does write one (:472-473). The move is still reconstructible, because lc_action.recommendation_id links to the attributed REJECTED approval_decision and its audit. This is audit-trail debt. (2) Correction to the side note: if moveAction returned false, the action would stay REVIEWED. It would keep the unique lc_action_live_uq slot (V0077:164-166) and block any new action on that listing until someone runs a manual cancel (ListingActionService.java:455-470, LISTING_ACTION_PREPARE). That fails closed and is an availability issue, not a bypass. It also looks practically unreachable. No DB function bumps a REVIEWED action's version: the V0118 updates at :213 and :233 act only on APPROVED/APPROVED_NOT_LAUNCHABLE actions. A concurrent approve or cancel would either hit the recommendation version guard first (ApprovalService.java:177-178 via RecommendationRepository.java:135) or deadlock and roll back.
